milestone: M49 Headless Mode Pack Update Drive

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive execute one explicit Mode Pack selected-candidate fetch route from persisted session state.
Keeps the selected Mode Pack update pipeline inside Rust-owned run-control after registry selection.
Requires explicit selected-candidate fetch target, matching persisted route, current session sequence, and existing continuation authorization.
Persists normal run-session and drive evidence while replaying without duplicate fetch checkpoints or side effects.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with supporting progress for mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive can execute one fetch_selected_modepack_candidate_explicitly route step from a persisted run-session checkpoint by passing a bounded selected-candidate fetch target to existing continuation authority.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: headless.continue_once can fetch a selected candidate, but run-control could not cross this explicit route boundary while preserving session sequence, drive checkpoints, and replay-safe evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A long-running scheduled caller would still leave headless.run.* after registry selection and own out-of-band route sequencing before provenance verification can proceed.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M46.4 replaced active state, M47.1 rolled back active replacement, and M48.1 selected a registry update candidate; M49.1 binds the already-existing selected-candidate fetch into run-control.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends existing headless.run.advance/headless.run.drive request handling and delegates to existing headless.continue_once rather than adding a new RPC.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It reuses bounded run-control results and existing selected-candidate fetch evidence instead of creating a summary/report surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates a persisted fetch route, derives progress from the checkpoint, delegates the fetch target through existing continuation authority, records run-control evidence, and replays without refetching.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can keep the first explicit Mode Pack update route boundary inside durable run-control instead of manually stitching continuation calls between sessions.
answers.milestone_progress: M49 gains its first route-drive vertical slice and establishes the bounded pattern for later distinct Mode Pack update route boundaries.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M49.1 updates the current and archived value manifests for the selected-candidate fetch route-drive phase.

exit_criteria: headless.run.advance accepts a bounded modepack_selected_candidate_fetch_target only for an existing session whose persisted next route is fetch_selected_modepack_candidate_explicitly
headless.run.drive passes the same bounded target through one runtime-owned routed advance and stops at the next explicit route boundary
runtime delegates selected-candidate fetch work to existing headless.continue_once authority and preserves run-session replay behavior
VSIX protocol validators accept the bounded run-control target and reject raw/unknown fields
behavior_evidence: Rust compile checks cover the new protocol/runtime request plumbing
VSIX protocol tests validate run-control params with selected-candidate fetch target and raw field rejection
Follow-up validation must include behavior tests for success, replay, wrong route, missing target, and mismatch denial before PR merge
